decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch the right gripper toward the basket, keeping the left arm parked and preserving elbow-up continuity.
Approach above the rear basket egg while rotating toward a downward grasp; leave clearance before descending.
Align the open gripper over the rear egg and lower with small increments; final grasp depth will be checked in RGB.
Lower the last few centimeters around the rear egg and close; retention remains to be verified by lifting.
Lift with the right gripper closed and check that a single egg remains between the fingers.
Carry the visibly retained egg toward the holder, angling the fingers inward while keeping the right EE on its own side.
Visually align the held egg with the rear-right cup and lower gradually, keeping the fingers closed.
Lower toward the cup bottom with a small rightward alignment correction; verify seating before opening.
Open over the rear-right cup and retreat upward; contact limited the last descent, so check that the egg settles into the holder.
One egg is visible in the front-right cup. Return above the basket's upper remaining egg with the gripper open.
Descend over the upper remaining basket egg, using the wrist view to check the approach before grasping.
Center the fingers farther forward around the second egg, lower slightly, then close for a test lift.
Lift the second egg clear of the basket with the gripper held closed, then begin turning toward the holder.
Carry the retained second egg above the empty rear-right cup, avoiding the egg already in the front-right cup.
The second egg slipped onto the table beside the holder. Reorient vertically and approach it with the gripper open for recovery.
Follow the rolled egg to its current table position and descend with open fingers, checking centering before closing.
Back away from contact and turn the open jaws to avoid the nearby holder and basket during the table-egg recovery.
Lower with the reoriented jaws over the loose egg, compensating for the EE-to-fingertip offset.
Reduce the open-jaw footprint near the basket, then make a shallow grasp attempt on the loose egg without forcing the descent.
The loose egg is outside the closed jaws. Reopen and shift toward it in the wrist view before another grasp.
The egg is now centered between the open fingers. Lower gently and close around it for recovery.
Test the loose-egg grasp with a straight upward lift, keeping the gripper closed and avoiding rotation.
The egg was not retained. Correct the lateral fingertip offset to the right and reapproach with a moderate opening.
Use the wrist image to move the jaw midpoint onto the egg, then close after a shallow descent.
The egg still appears below the grasp plane. Reopen and lower to surround its sides rather than pinch above it.
Shift the grasp plane toward the egg's lower wrist-image position, close around its sides, and begin a short retention test.
Clear the contact and restore a vertical approach over the loose egg before another carefully centered descent.
After the tracking interruption, close the empty jaws and withdraw straight upward with small steps to clear nearby contact.
Use an intermediate upward pose to restore IK continuity, closing the empty gripper to reduce collision footprint.
Upward withdrawal is obstructed. Retreat diagonally toward the robot and away from the holder to clear the contact before retrying.
Release any incidental contact and withdraw straight upward in very small increments, replanning from the interrupted pose.
Bridge the last accepted target and actual pose to pass continuity checks, opening before a slow upward retreat.
The arm is not following upward withdrawal. Try a small rightward, rearward escape away from the holder before another approach.
Pause at an intermediate target with open jaws to let tracking settle before attempting further recovery.
Unwind the wrist toward its earlier grasp orientation while retracting slowly; repeated translation-only withdrawal has not cleared the obstruction.
Bridge the tracking residual, then withdraw rearward at nearly constant height to clear the holder and basket before lifting.
Continue the slow rearward escape while pitching the fingertips upward to clear table-level contact.
Tracking has recovered. Move above the loose egg from the clear rear side with an angled, moderately open grasp.
Visually center the loose egg between the jaws while lowering from the unobstructed rear approach.
Make the final lateral centering correction and close around the loose egg without further downward pressure.
Test retention with a small straight lift; keep the gripper closed and verify the egg moves with the fingers.
The egg did not lift. Reset to the previously effective vertical grasp orientation above its head-camera location before descending.
Descend vertically over the isolated egg with a narrower opening to avoid the adjacent basket rim.
Narrow the jaws to clear the basket rim, advance over the egg, and make a short controlled descent.
Close the jaws and retreat toward the clear front area, relieving the basket-side contact before attempting a lower grasp.
Withdraw upward while pitching clear of the table contact, then move back toward the basket's remaining eggs.
Approach the front basket egg from above with the successful near-vertical grasp orientation.
Advance the open fingers over the front egg while descending, using the wrist image for final centering.
Close around the front basket egg after a shallow descent, then begin a small straight retention lift.
Lift straight upward with closed fingers to verify whether the front egg is securely retained.
The previous grasp was empty. Reopen and realign over the egg's new position before a slower, better-centered grasp.
The egg is now between the open jaws; make a small lateral correction and close without advancing past it.
Test this centered grasp with a gentle straight lift and no wrist rotation.
The egg slipped from a shallow pinch. Follow its new position and approach deeper with a reduced opening to clear the basket.
Correct the jaw center toward the egg in the wrist view at the deeper height, then close without further descent.
Lift slowly without rotation to test the deeper grasp while keeping the jaws closed.
Reopen and adjust slightly left and rearward around the egg, stopping before closure to inspect the finger alignment.
Bring the egg upward and centrally between the finger faces in the wrist image, then close slowly without further descent.
Lift only a few centimeters at low speed while keeping the fingers closed, checking the apparent side grasp for retention.
The egg appears retained. Lift clear and begin a gentle transfer toward the holder without changing the grasp orientation.
Transport the retained egg slowly toward the empty rear cup, adding only a gentle inward tilt for reach.
Continue the gentle carry over the empty rear-right cup, lowering only to an above-holder staging height.
The carried egg slipped beside the holder. Withdraw from the lid and approach that egg using a fixed wrist angle for a short recovery transfer.
Lower toward the nearby loose egg at a fixed angle, narrowing the opening to reduce interference with the holder.
Back off the holder contact and turn the jaws so their opening will run alongside, rather than across, the holder edge.
Approach the loose egg beside the holder with the jaws nearly parallel to its edge; inspect before the final grasp.
Center the nearby egg laterally between the parallel jaws, then close slowly at fixed height.
The jaws closed short of the egg. Reopen and advance carefully along the finger direction to surround its sides.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for unexecuted motion; align over the egg and close gradually.
The egg lies left of the closed jaws in the wrist view. Reopen and correct along the jaw-closing axis before retrying.
The loose egg escaped the grasp. Withdraw and return toward the last basket egg, restoring the earlier grasp orientation gradually.
Finish aligning the open gripper vertically above the remaining basket egg, keeping clearance during wrist rotation.
Descend over the last basket egg with a small wrist-view centering correction, keeping the jaws open.
Move the grasp plane forward to surround the egg's center rather than its near end, then close gradually.
